instruction: Create a text file at ~/paper_list.txt listing all PDF filenames in ~/Documents/Papers/, one filename per line, sorted alphabetically.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to extract first authors from 4 PDFs and create Excel table. Installed poppler-utils, converted PDFs to text, read author info, started writing Python/openpyxl script but ran out of 50 turns before completing the xlsx file. Also misidentified first author of zhang_appagent.pdf.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, install packages (apt-get), use pdftotext to convert PDFs, read text files with head/grep, write Python scripts in terminal, use openpyxl for Excel creation
metadata.failure_analysis: Model spent too many turns on installation waits and type+Enter cycles. Misidentified first author of AppAgent paper (Gang Yu instead of Chi Zhang). Ran out of 50-turn limit before saving the xlsx file.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original multi-step task into simple file listing. No PDF parsing needed - just ls and sort. Tests terminal usage and file creation within demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires listing PDF filenames alphabetically in a text file. Getter reads the text file from VM, metric checks each line matches expected sorted filename with partial credit (0.25 per correct filename in correct position).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the target file /home/user/paper_list.txt and returns content as a list of stripped, non-empty lines
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (expected.get('expected_lines')) - proper handling for type='rule'
Expected values are correct: the 4 PDF filenames sorted alphabetically (deng_mind2web.pdf, koh_visualwebarena.pdf, niu_screenagent.pdf, zhang_appagent.pdf)
All instruction requirements are covered: file at correct path, correct filenames, one per line, sorted alphabetically
Partial credit scoring (0.25 per correct line in correct position) is sensible for this 4-item task
Minor: fuzzy matching with 'in' operator (exp_clean in actual_clean) is slightly permissive but unlikely to cause false positives in practice
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using exact match only (remove the 'exp_clean in actual_clean' fallback) to avoid potential false positives where a line contains the expected filename as a substring
